channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan adjusts personal assistant payment for families with multiple disabled members
item.description: Starting September 1, 2026, Kyrgyzstan will change how personal assistants are paid. Assistants caring for two or more disabled individuals within the same family will receive full payment for each person. This change aims to improve care quality for children and adults with disabilities requiring constant supervision.

item.title: New Justice Minister appointed in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Almaz Aiylchiev has been appointed Acting Minister of Justice in Kyrgyzstan, replacing Ayaz Bayetov who was transferred to another position. Aiylchiev currently heads the Legal Support Department and serves as Deputy Head of the Legal Support Directorate of the President and Cabinet of Ministers. His candidacy requires Zhogorku Kenesh approval.

item.title: Tajikistan hosts forum on preserving language, culture, and historical heritage
item.description: A scientific forum on "Independent Tajikistan — the connecting link of Aryan civilization" was held in Dushanbe, organized by the World Association of Tajiks and Persian-speaking Peoples "Payvand." Over 230 guests from 27 countries attended the event, which focused on preserving language, culture, and historical heritage.

item.title: Kyrgyzpharmatsiya discusses pharmaceutical product supplies from Uzbekistan in Tashkent
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan explored expanding cooperation in the pharmaceutical sector, including Uzbek product supplies to Kyrgyzstan. Representatives from both countries discussed their organizations' work and potential future interactions. Particular attention was given to increasing pharmaceutical product imports from Uzbekistan to Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Tightens Entry Rules for Foreigners Overstaying Visas
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will deny re-entry to foreigners who exceed their permitted stay, with the ban duration matching their visa-free period. The Cabinet of Ministers updated regulations, with an automated system calculating stay duration. Exceptions exist for spouses and children of Kyrgyz citizens.

item.title: Uzbek Builders to Participate in 200km Railway Construction in Serbia
item.description: Uzbekistan Railways will participate in its first major European railway projects, constructing a 200-kilometer railway in Serbia. This agreement was reached during an intergovernmental commission meeting in Belgrade.

item.title: UN Human Rights Chief Concerned by Over 60 Global Conflicts and AI in Warfare
item.description: The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights expressed deep concern over more than 60 ongoing global conflicts, a level not seen since WWII. He also voiced alarm about artificial intelligence in warfare, particularly autonomous weapons, calling for strong safety guarantees.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Updates Foreigner Registration Rules, Abolishing Previous Regulations
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has approved a new procedure for registering foreign citizens and stateless persons. The new rules aim to streamline entry and stay for foreigners, establishing separate registration-free periods for citizens of different countries. Previous regulations from 2016 and subsequent amendments are now void.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Establishes Glacier and Issyk-Kul Lake Protection Fund
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has decreed the creation of a fund to protect and preserve Kyrgyzstan's glaciers and Issyk-Kul Lake. The fund will seek international and donor financing for projects on climate adaptation, glacier degradation reduction, and ecosystem preservation. The Cabinet of Ministers must define the fund's structure and financing by October 2026.

item.title: Removal from Social Registry Does Not Mean Poverty Reduction, Says IHMA
item.description: The IHMA Social Protection Inspectorate is conducting oversight on families removed from the social registry. The inspectorate is examining whether decisions align with established criteria and procedures. This indicates that removal from the registry does not automatically signify a reduction in poverty.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev begins official visit to Serbia
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and his wife have arrived in Belgrade for an official visit. They were met by Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić and his wife at the airport. The main events, including high-level negotiations and a business forum, are scheduled for the next day, with a package of bilateral documents expected to be signed.

item.title: Kazakhstan launches women-only train carriages on Almaty-Tashkent route
item.description: Kazakhstan's national railway company is introducing women-only train carriages on the Almaty-Tashkent route starting October 1. Tickets will be sold only to women, and only female attendants will serve them. Boys up to age 7 are allowed with women. This service is popular on domestic routes.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Higher Education System Undergoing Major Reforms and Expansion
item.description: Uzbekistan's higher education system is undergoing significant transformation, with a focus on accessibility, quality, and scientific potential. The number of higher education institutions has grown from 77 to 205 in ten years, and student enrollment has tripled. Private sector involvement has led to the establishment of 74 non-state universities.

item.title: Airport emergency rescue teams compete in Bukhara
item.description: Uzbekistan's airport emergency and rescue services competed in fire and applied sports in Bukhara. Teams demonstrated speed, strength, and professional skills in three disciplines, including climbing a training tower and a fire relay. The Urgench airport team won first place, followed by Bukhara and Andijan.

item.title: Tashkent prepares for autumn-winter season with focus on utility readiness
item.description: Tashkent held a working meeting to prepare the city for the autumn-winter period, ensuring safe and uninterrupted operation. Participants focused on the readiness of utility services and public service systems for increased seasonal loads. Measures to ensure resident safety during cold weather, including fire and carbon monoxide poisoning prevention, were also discussed.

item.title: Uzbekistan imports less but more expensive gasoline; prices surged in recent months
item.description: Uzbekistan imported 721.5 million liters of gasoline from January to August, a 41.2% increase year-on-year. The import value rose 48.6% to $437.4 million. While the average import price per 1000 liters increased by 5.3%, prices surged by 73% from April to August, with import volumes decreasing significantly in July and August.

item.title: Filmmaker Aybek Dayyrbekov appointed Deputy Minister of Culture in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Filmmaker and screenwriter Aybek Dayyrbekov has been appointed Deputy Minister of Culture, Information, and Youth Policy in Kyrgyzstan. The decision was signed by the head of the Cabinet of Ministers, Adylbek Kasymaliev.

item.title: New electric trains to operate between Khiva and Bukhara in Uzbekistan
item.description: New electric trains will be launched on the Khiva-Bukhara route in Uzbekistan. Each five-car train will have 415 economy-class seats and complete the journey in over 4.5 hours.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev Arrives in Serbia for Official Visit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has arrived in Serbia for an official visit. He was welcomed at the Nikola Tesla International Airport by Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić and his wife. The visit aims to strengthen bilateral relations between the two countries.

item.title: Russia and North Korea Open First Border Bridge Over Tuman River
item.description: Russia and North Korea have inaugurated their first road bridge across the Tuman River, connecting the two countries. The 1-kilometer bridge, named after Soviet officer Yakov Novichenko, was opened via video link by Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin and North Korean Premier Pak Thae Song.

item.title: New Chinese electric train to operate between Khiva and Bukhara
item.description: A CR200J electric train manufactured by China's CRRC Dalian will begin service between Khiva and Bukhara on September 9. The route extends the existing service from Urgench airport to the Bukhara-1 station. Services will run six days a week, with one weekly trip to Tashkent starting September 14.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia Identify Promising Areas for Digitalization Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan and Russia held a roundtable on digital transformation, focusing on cooperation in digital technologies, artificial intelligence, and the digital economy. Participants discussed expanding the use of these technologies in the economy, social sphere, and government. The initiative to form a joint digital ecosystem between the two countries was highlighted.

item.title: President of Uzbekistan Departs for Official Visit to Belgrade
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan, Shavkat Mirziyoyev, has departed for Serbia on an official visit at the invitation of President Aleksandar Vučić. The program includes high-level negotiations and a business forum. Discussions will focus on strengthening multifaceted Uzbek-Serbian cooperation, with a package of documents expected to be signed.

item.title: Bishkek city hall reviews post-SCO and VIK summit tasks for urban services
item.description: Bishkek city hall has reviewed the outcomes of major international events hosted in the capital and outlined future tasks for city services and district administrations. The mayor emphasized the need for continued infrastructure development, including road and facade renovations, and ordered an audit of expenses to ensure targeted fund utilization and quality control.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ranks 61st in Global Peace Index
item.description: Kyrgyzstan secured 61st place out of 163 countries in the Global Peace Index 2026. The country scored 1.853 points, according to the Institute for Economics & Peace. Neighboring countries also ranked: Kazakhstan (44th), Tajikistan (47th), Uzbekistan (37th), and Turkmenistan (66th).

item.title: Kyrgyzstan ranks 61st in the 2026 Global Peace Index
item.description: Kyrgyzstan secured 61st place out of 163 countries in the 2026 Global Peace Index, with 1.853 points. Iceland leads the ranking, followed by New Zealand and Switzerland. Other Central Asian nations included Kazakhstan (44th), Tajikistan (47th), Uzbekistan (37th), and Turkmenistan (66th).

item.title: Responsibility for Nuclear Safety Violations to Be Strengthened in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's legislative chamber discussed amendments to laws concerning industrial, radiation, and nuclear safety. The proposed changes aim to improve state supervision, align with international standards, and strengthen measures to prevent violations. The bill clarifies the powers of the Committee for Industrial, Radiation, and Nuclear Safety and the Inspectorate for Mining and Geological Supervision.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Loans to individuals approach 240 trillion soums, with mortgages leading
item.description: As of August 1, 2026, outstanding loans to individuals in Uzbekistan reached nearly 240 trillion soums, an 8.9% increase since the start of the year. Mortgages constitute the largest share at 36.8%, totaling 88.1 trillion soums. Microloans follow, with an outstanding balance of 51.1 trillion soums.

item.title: Israel Launches New Strikes on Lebanon, Killing 11
item.description: Israel conducted further strikes on Lebanon, resulting in 11 fatalities. Lebanon reported that the strikes by Israeli forces were carried out without prior online evacuation warnings to the civilian population.

item.title: Turkmenistan elected chair of Landlocked Developing Countries Group for 2027-2028
item.description: Turkmenistan has been elected as the chair of the Group of Landlocked Developing Countries (LLDCs) for the 2027-2028 period. Azerbaijan will serve as vice-chair. This position will allow Turkmenistan to coordinate the group's activities, representing 32 developing nations, in areas like energy and transport.

item.title: Uzbekistan and China expand cooperation in environmental education and green talent development
item.description: A delegation from Uzbekistan visited China to discuss environmental education and training of "green" personnel. Agreements were reached to enhance collaboration between educational and research institutions. Memoranda of understanding were signed between Green University and Chinese counterparts for student/faculty exchange and joint research on satellite data for environmental monitoring.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia to Elevate Political Dialogue to Practical Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Serbia on September 7-8 to strengthen bilateral relations. The visit aims to transform existing political trust into concrete economic outcomes, including trade, investment, and logistical cooperation, building on recent diplomatic and economic engagement.

item.title: White House Website Features Anti-Immigrant Video Games
item.description: The White House website has launched anti-immigrant video games, drawing criticism from human rights advocates. One game involves catching migrants crossing the Rio Grande, while another simulates building a wall on the U.S.-Mexico border.

item.title: Uzbekistan ranks third among central banks buying gold year-to-date
item.description: Despite selling nearly one ton of gold in July, Uzbekistan remains a major buyer, ranking third globally for net purchases since the start of the year, totaling 40 tons. Central banks worldwide increased reserves by 23 tons in July, with China and Poland being the largest buyers.

item.title: Kyrgyz MP appointed CIS IPA observer coordinator for Russian Duma elections
item.description: Gula Kozhokulova, a member of Kyrgyzstan's Jogorku Kenesh, has been appointed coordinator of international observers from the CIS Interparliamentary Assembly for the upcoming Russian State Duma elections. The observer group will include representatives from CIS parliaments and experts. The elections are scheduled for September 18-20, 2026.

item.title: Kyrgyz MP Gulya Kozhokulova appointed CIS election observer coordinator
item.description: Gulya Kozhokulova, a member of the Jogorku Kenesh committee on international affairs, defense, security, and migration, has been appointed coordinator of international observers from the CIS Interparliamentary Assembly for the Russian State Duma elections. The observers will monitor the elections at the invitation of the State Duma Chairman.

item.title: Washington Governor congratulates Uzbekistan on opening first consulate in Seattle
item.description: Washington Governor Bob Ferguson congratulated Uzbekistan on the opening of its first consulate general in Seattle. He emphasized that the new diplomatic mission will create new opportunities for trade, investment, technology, innovation, education, and scientific research.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Dollar exchange rate rises after three-day decline
item.description: The dollar exchange rate in Uzbekistan has increased following a three-day period of decline. The Central Bank announced the official exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective September 8.

item.title: Gas extraction begins at new 'Patron' gas condensate field in Qashqadaryo region
item.description: Gas extraction has commenced at the new 'Patron' gas condensate field in the Mirishkor district of Uzbekistan's Qashqadaryo region. The first exploration well was connected to the gas pipeline on September 2. The Ministry of Energy refuted social media reports of a gas explosion, clarifying that the video showed the well's testing and commissioning process.

item.title: Uzbekistan to mandate state registration for medical professionals by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to introduce state registration for medical and pharmaceutical workers. The system will be voluntary from 2027 to 2030 and mandatory thereafter. Unregistered specialists will be unable to practice medicine or pharmacy. A unified electronic registry will be created, integrating data on qualifications and professional activities.
